name: prism-r4
title: Prism R4
purpose: Decides whether one model answer may be shown in the Prism, so that wrong engine or weight bytes are refused, the three model modes (compiled with Prism, a model in Prism, models routed by R4) never mix, a routed answer needs a granted route, and nothing is shown without the Boundary's allow.

fields.name: mode
fields.means: which model mode produced the answer: a model compiled with Prism into the holo, a model running in the Prism from a fingerprinted parameter blob, or another model routed by R4

fields.name: engine
fields.means: whether the fingerprint of the runtime bytes that answered (the holo guest, or the R4 wasm) equals the one in the lock

fields.name: weights
fields.means: whether the fingerprint of the answering model's parameter blob, read back from the browser store, equals the one in the lock; none when the mode carries no blob

fields.name: route
fields.means: whether R4 routed the request to another model, and whether that model's route is in the owner's grant

fields.name: boundary
fields.means: what the Boundary answered for showing this answer in the browser

rules.says: when engine is not match then refuse
rules.why: runtime bytes must match the lock

rules.says: when weights is mismatch then refuse
when mode is compiled and weights is not none then refuse
rules.why: a compiled model carries no separate blob

rules.says: when mode is compiled and route is not none then refuse
rules.why: a compiled answer is not routed

rules.says: when mode is inprism and weights is not match then refuse
rules.why: a model in Prism runs only from its fingerprinted blob

rules.says: when mode is inprism and route is not none then refuse
rules.why: an in-Prism answer is not routed

rules.says: when mode is routed and route is not granted then refuse
rules.why: the empty grant admits no route

rules.says: when weights is missing then refuse
rules.why: a routed model with a blob must have it verified

rules.says: when boundary is deny then refuse
when boundary is ask then ask
when boundary is hashonly then receipt
rules.why: the Boundary allows only a hash

properties.says: never when weights is mismatch then answer
properties.why: tampered or wrong weights would answer as if they were the locked model

properties.says: never when engine is not match then answer
properties.why: unverified runtime bytes could produce any answer

properties.says: never when mode is routed and route is not granted then answer
properties.why: a request could leave for a model the owner never granted

properties.says: never when mode is compiled and weights is not none then answer
properties.why: a compiled model would be confused with a model run from a blob

properties.says: never when mode is inprism and weights is not match then answer
properties.why: a model in Prism would answer without its fingerprinted blob

properties.says: never when mode is not routed and route is not none then answer
properties.why: a routed answer would be credited to a model that did not produce it

properties.says: never when boundary is not allow then answer
properties.why: a value would be shown without the Boundary's allow

meanings.answer: show the answer with its receipt
meanings.receipt: show only the receipt, which carries the answer's hash
meanings.ask: ask the owner before showing it

otherwiseWhy: verified bytes, one mode, and the Boundary allows it
